convoLines.text: "My cut needs a second pair of hands. Could you clean it out for me? Please."
"It's getting worse, not better. If it festers I'm no good to anyone — can't haul, can't hunt, can't watch. Just clean it out and wrap it tight."
Move next to them, on the same side of the Haven door, to help.
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
"There's more, but that's for another fire."
"You're really going to make me say it again?" Shanice rubs their face. "Fine — but it's the same truth as last time."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"You look handy. What did you do with your hands, before?"
"Useful. Everything useful matters now. I mean that as a compliment."
"No, yeah, of course. Forget I asked." They won't forget. They'll just stop asking.
"Still on that wound care."
"Alright — I should get back to it."
"Okay. I'll manage on my own."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"My wound needs a second pair of hands. Could you take a look?"
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
"an old trapline — I'll show you on the map sometime. It's real."
"Jian owed me a favor. I keep thinking about collecting. Stupid."
"Not right now. I've got my own things to handle."
"I check everyone's shoes for wear. It doesn't bring anyone back. It just keeps my hands from shaking."
"Nobody says Jian's name right yet. We will. Give it a few days."
"Still on what's been happening."
You show them Spicebush — where it grows, how to tell it apart. They nod slowly, committing it to memory. "Good to know. Really good to know."
"Okay. We'll pick this up later."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"...Think about it? I'll be around."
"This was good." They mean it.
"I asked Jian about the pantry run — Jian's gone. Still need hands. Are you in?"
"The stores won't stretch past tomorrow, and I'm not choosing who eats. I know the east treeline — come with me and we'll fill packs before dark."
Your partner is inside the Haven hall. Go through the door to meet them.
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
Their eyes do the math before their mouth does. You can see the calculation happening.
Quiet for a long time. Then, barely audible: "I took 1× Stone. I won't do it again."
They glance at the fire, then back. The quiet doesn't seem to bother them.
They settle — not warm, not cold. Just two people talking.
"Right. I get it." A beat — and then the subject is closed. They won't raise it again.
"Still on that wound care."
"I should go. You know where to find me."
"Forget I asked. I'll figure it out."
They nod, already turning away.
"We never finished talking about that wound care — we got cut off, 4 days back. 'Alright — I should get back to it.'"
"It's already handled. Thank you for asking."
"Like I said — Still on that wound care."
You show them Spicebush — where it grows, how to tell it apart. "Huh." They turn it over in their mind. "I'll remember that one."
A warmth settles over the conversation — they lean in a little.
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
"My cut needs a second pair of hands. Could you take a look?"
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"I should go. You know where to find me."
"...Think about it? I'll be around."
"This was good." They mean it.
"About whether you're angry — Are you angry? At whoever did this. At the sky. At anything. Simple as that."
"Good. Anger's fuel. Just — point it somewhere useful. Anyway."
"Still on whether you're angry."
"Okay. Yeah. I trust you."
"...I should say, I trade in what I know. My knowledge for yours. Or food, if you're short on secrets."
"Good question." "I dreamed Tom was still here. Woke up angry at the dream. Stupid."
"I keep turning over the last thing Tom said to me. I can't tell if I'm remembering it right, and that's somehow the worst part."
"A name. Okay." You say it out loud, trying the shape of it:
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
"Nobody says Tom's name right yet. We will. Give it a few days."
You show them Spicebush — where it grows, how to tell it apart. Their eyes widen. "I never knew that."
"Sure. I'll be around."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"Can we talk?" Shanice doesn't wait for an answer. "We need to discuss how things are run here."
"Help me haul something back? Too much for one."
It's quiet at the cache spot. Shanice doesn't say much. Sometimes that's the whole point.
"About this wound — the need hasn't gone anywhere. I'm still asking."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
"That night — I put down Static at the treeline. I keep hearing it when I try to sleep."
"Okay. Yeah. I trust you."
"Okay. We'll pick this up later."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"...Think about it? I'll be around."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"About the pantry run — I hate to ask twice, but it's still open. Will you?"
"The stores won't stretch past tomorrow, and I'm not choosing who eats. Nobody's worked the east treeline in days. We'll fill packs before dark."
Your partner is inside the Haven hall. Go through the door to meet them.
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
"Good question." "You asked me that before. It's a different question now." "That night — I stood down Big Big at the treeline — it ran. I keep hearing it when I try to sleep."
"That's the whole of it. Sorry."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
They glance at the fire, then back. The quiet doesn't seem to bother them.
"Good question." "I'd follow you out past the treeline. Don't tell the others — they'd want to come too."
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
"People here talk. What they say about you when you're not at the fire — that's the real answer to your question."
"Still on each other."
"Right. Go on, then."
"...Think about it? I'll be around."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"You told me your trade. I've been watching your hands since — they know things."
"There's more, but that's for another fire."
They nod slowly, not quite done, not quite continuing.
"Still on that personal stuff."
"Yeah? What's up?"
"I asked James about this wound — James's gone. Still need hands. Are you in?"
"It's getting worse, not better. If it festers I'm no good to anyone — can't haul, can't hunt, can't watch. Just clean it out and wrap it tight."
You spend time tending them. This was care, not a promise of a cure.
"Alright — I should get back to it."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"It's been a while. Glad we circled back to that foraging help."
"This was good." They mean it.
"I hate to ask this, but I'm feverish, a cut gone hot and angry. I need help. Please."
"It's not just the cut anymore, it's in the blood, I can feel it climbing. I need someone who knows wounds."
Move next to them, on the same side of the Haven door, to help.
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
"James owed me a favor. I keep thinking about collecting. Stupid."
"Not right now. I've got my own things to handle."
You show them Spicebush — where it grows, how to tell it apart. A short laugh. "And I've been walking past it for weeks."
"I should go. You know where to find me."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"...Think about it? I'll be around."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."

lastSay: d76: Nobody's talking much. The fire feels smaller tonight.
d76: NATHAN — GONE. 1 open question closed unanswered.
d76: 🕯️ Nathan Lee is dead — the wild. The village stops. Somebody screams. Somebody else starts digging.
d76: What Nathan kept close goes into the ground with them — keepsakes are buried, never taken from the body.
d76: No one is left to pick up the Codex. The village dies out — quietly, the way villages do. The season ends here.
